Rooms.Name: End of the Clay Road
Rooms.Description:
The mighty clay road turns into lesser, but still well traveled
roads here. You feel a surge run through your body as you look east
into the lands that turned Rome into its mighty empire.

Exits.Description:
The Northern Road, linking Rome with Midgaard and other cities,
beckons.
The mighty clay road leads off in this direction.

Rooms.Name: Clay Road
Rooms.Description:
You travel upon an East-West road wide enough for 30 men to march
abreast. The road is heavy with traffic, both foot and wagons, yet
it is hard and smooth and well drained.

Exits.Description: The broad clay road stretches eastward to unknown regions.
In the far distance you can see the twin spires of Rome's East Gate.

Rooms.Name: Clay Road
Rooms.Description:
In the distance, to the west, you eyes catch the splendors of a
mighty city.  The road is congested with nobles and their huge
retinues of servants traveling from country estates into the city for
commerce, and with traders bringing treasures and goods for trade from
exotic locations.

Exits.Description: The clay road continues its straight path east as far as you can see.
The road ahead is lined with coffins and sarcophagi.

Rooms.Name: Clay Road
Rooms.Description:
On both sides of the road lie gravesites.  Large statues adorn
the final resting places of famous and not so famous Romans who have
passed over the river Styx.  To the northwest you can see a funeral
procession with at least a dozen professional mourners.  If someone
important has just died there will be lavish banquets and
entertainments tomorrow, so hurry into the city!

Exits.Description: A wide, straight road goes east as far as you can see.
Far west you can see the spires of Rome's East Gate.

Rooms.Name: Clay Road East of Rome
Rooms.Description:
Burial within the limited confines of the city of Rome is not
permitted, so the Romans have interred their dead in above-the-ground
coffins called sarcophagi.  The sarcophagi are decorated with
elaborately carved scenes from the person's life.

Exits.Description: A wide, hard packed clay road heads for the hills!
A wide, hard packed clay road heads for the city.

Rooms.Name: The Field of Mars
Rooms.Description:
On the northern side of the road stretches what is known as the
Field of Mars, a training ground for the mighty Roman soldier.  The
army is open to Roman citizens (males who own land) and is an
opportunity for a man to bring glory and a regular salary home to his
family.  Being soft is frowned upon even for non-combatants, and so
this area is often used by non-soldiers to develop strong muscles and
hard bodies.

Exits.Description: A narrow path through a lovely meadow starts here and heads north.
A broad clay road heads for parts unknown.

You see in the near distance, two tall spires that might be part of
the
gate to Rome.

Rooms.Name: Before Rome
Rooms.Description:
You travel upon an East-West road wide enough for 30 men to march
abreast. When a victorious general returns to Rome to (modestly)
receive honors due him, his army marches ahead of him down this grand
road.  You can see that it is packed hard through heavy use. To the
west stand the Gates of Rome inviting you to enter and partake of all
the glory and splendor that is Rome.

Exits.Description:
A wide clay road lined with sarcophagi of all varieties heads away
from
Rome.
The Gates of Rome!

Rooms.Name: The East Gate of Rome
Rooms.Description:
You are standing inside of the eastern gate of Rome. There are two
tall spires built into the city wall, from which the guards can see
the whole eastern side of the city. To the east, there is a heavily
used packed clay road that leads out of Rome. Another road leads
westward into the city.  A third, small narrow walkway leads south.

Exits.Description: A broad and well-traveled clay road leads east out of the city.

A narrow paved walkway leads south along the city wall past some
shops.
via Petrus leads into the city.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
There are two tall spires on either side of the gate and are
constantly manned by the city guards.  They are made of stone and stand
about 40 feet tall.

The gate is fabricated from iron and has been designed to keep
intruders out of the city.

Rooms.Name: via Petrus
Rooms.Description:
The clay road has become a well-paved road made from stone brought
in from the surrounding countryside.  Rome is a crowded, exciting city
with a population close to a million.  You are surrounded by buildings
of all types and sizes.  Just west of here there is an enormous white
marble building.  Many citizens, freedmen and slaves are going in and
out of the building.  To the east you see the East Gate of Rome, and
south of here there is a small greengrocers.

Exits.Description:
Going east you would need to leave Rome.  Why would you want to do
that?
The dim cool innards of a green grocers
via Petrus continues into the heart of Rome.

Rooms.Name: The Green Grocers
Rooms.Description:
The produce sold at this little shop changes daily depending upon
what has been brought in from the surrounding countryside or from
further afield.  The citizens love lavish banquets and new and
unusual things to eat.  The grocer, a former slave able to buy his
freedom from his profits at the store, has managed to build up a large
clientele for his goods.

Exits.Description: The magnificence of via Petrus is just out the door.

Rooms.Name: via Petrus
Rooms.Description:
You are surrounded by the noise, the odors and movement of the
densely populated city of Rome.  Just west of you a constant
procession of well-dressed Roman citizens and their slaves enter and
leave the huge formal bathhouse.  To the south some stairs lead up into
a small apartment building, and just east of here you can see the
spires of the East Gate.

Exits.Description: At a short distance you see the East Gate of Rome.
A set of dark steps lead up into an apartment building.
via Petrus continues past a large white building.

Rooms.Name: via Petrus by the Baths
Rooms.Description:
You are standing before a grand set of marble steps leading up to an
enormous building made of white stone.  Statues of lesser known Roman
gods stand at several levels up the graceful shallow steps.  The
street continues east to the gate, west through a large arch, and there
is an entrance to the south to a small curio shop.

Exits.Description: The busy thoroughfare that is via Petrus is packed with citizens.
A dim and unusually dusty shop lies south of here.
via Petrus continues to a large commemorative arch.
Steps lead to the baths.

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Arched Entrance
Rooms.Description:
White stucco leads to a highly embellished green archway over a
white marble floor.  This is the entryway to the largest bath-house in
Rome, and the most elegant, although there are over a hundred others.
This particular bath-house allows only men.

Exits.Description: An attended cloakroom is just to the north of you.
Broad marble steps lead down to a busy street.

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Cloakroom
Rooms.Description:
Romans disrobe down to their loincloths here, leaving their
belongings either with a cloakroom attendant or one of their personal
servants.  The latter is the wiser course for those who wish to keep
all of their belongings!  The room is spacious and lovely.  To the east
you will find the tepidarium, where you can begin to warm your body.

Exits.Description:
The echoes of a large stone room and a faint wave of humidity head
for
you from the east.
Through an arched entryway you can see the busy street.

Men are emerging in small groups from the west, looking for their
belongings.

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Tepidarium
Rooms.Description:
You have entered a warm room with a small pool of warm water.  In
the center of the pool is a statue of a water sprite holding a large
vessel of water.  Water is pouring from the vessel into the pool.
The room's graceful domed ceiling is painted with bright colors.  From
here you may go to the cloakroom to the south, the gymnasium to the
north, or directly west to the caldarium, the hot room.

Exits.Description:
The air coming in from the north is warmer and more humid.  It looks
like another room with a pool.

Through the open archway you can see an attendant retrieving clothing
for a noble patron.

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Warm Up
Rooms.Description:
The floor in this area is smooth, slick white marble squares, and
feels cool to your bare feet.  The walls have been decorated with
colorful mosaics depicting a graceful Apollo in various games.
Around you attendants watch while senators and other politicians and
nobles exercise their bodies, warming their muscles before bathing.

Exits.Description:
Fresh air and the grunts of men playing active sports come to you
from the open area north of here.
Another large room lies south.
Steep marble steps lead up to a library.

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Library
Rooms.Description:
The baths are a very social place.  This elegant bath house boasts
a large library where citizens may research legal matters or read
history, poetry, or other areas that might interest them.  The walls
are lined with scrolls, and there are several comfortable places to sit
while you read.  The only exit is down.

Exits.Description:
At the bottom of a long flight of steps you hear the splash of water
in the tepid pool and the sounds of men working out.

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Gymnasium East
Rooms.Description:
This exercise yard boasts an outdoor pool for bathing or swimming.
In the northeastern corner of the yard you can see young citizens
playfully wrestling, and to the west a game is being played with a
leather ball.  In the northwestern corner some men are soaking up
sunshine and becoming fashionably tanned.  The gymnasium continues to
the west.  The tepidarium lies south of here.

Exits.Description: Splashes and the echoes of laughter come to you from the Warmup room.
The gymnasium continues westwards.

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Gymnasium West
Rooms.Description:
Shouts and laughter greet you as you walk onto the western half of
the gymnasium yard.  A large group of citizens are playing a game
involving a small leather ball.  In a sunny corner some older men
appear to be playing dice.  When their bodies are very warm, they will
enter the caldarium just south of here.

Exits.Description: The wide grassy field continues full of men playing games.
A cloud of steam rises from what must be a very warm pool of water.

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Getting Clean
Rooms.Description:
Long, warm benches are lined up here for bathers to use.
Attendants are available for hire to give massages.  Warm oils are
rubbed into the skin, then scraped off with strigils, or scrapers of
various shapes and sizes.  The hot pool is south, the gymnasium is
north of here.

Exits.Description: Open air, sunshine and laughter beckon you outdoors.
A Roman hot tub awaits you.
A cloud of steam drifts from the Lanconicum

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Caldarium
Rooms.Description:
You can feel the sweat oozing from your pores due to the heat and
moisture of this room.  It is very tempting just to sink into the
water and drift off to sleep.  You may wish to take advantage of the
bathing attendants to become really clean.  They are armed with warm
oil and scrapers (strigils).

Exits.Description: Several bath attendants are giving massages and cleaning warm flesh.
A cool pool will finish off your bath.
Steam clean your pores in the Laconicum

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Laconicum
Rooms.Description:
A cloud of thick steam envelops you as you enter the laconicum, a
room primarily for invalids. Sneezes abound here, but it is difficult
to tell where people are due to the thick steam.

Exits.Description: Several slaves are waiting to clean your body or massage it.
Take a cooling dip

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Frigidarium
Rooms.Description:
Cool down here!  There is an enormous swimming pool in the middle
of an spacious open room.  This is the final stop before leaving the
baths, unless you wish to visit in the library or take advantage of one
of the servants to get your hair cut or other grooming services
performed on your now clean body.  A lovely arch leads to the cloak
room east of here.

Exits.Description:
You can head for the steam room from here, although the idea is to
heat up gradually, then cool off, not the reverse!

Through the arch you see someone stealing your clothing!  Stop!
Thief!!

Rooms.Name: The Baths - Marble Steps
Rooms.Description:
A series of wide shallow steps lead up to a gloriously arched
entranceway.  Whatever this building is, it is very busy.  There are
many small groups of men climbing and descending these stairs.  The
main street lies down the stairs, and the entrance to the building is
up.

Exits.Description:
Climb the stairs a bit further to the north and you will find
yourself standing in a magnificent arched entryway.
Descend the steps a bit to the busy street.

Rooms.Name: Triumphal Arch - Victory over Shaalziran'dar
Rooms.Description:
This magnificent arch stands in the middle of a small square,
celebrating the Roman victory over the drow of Shaalziran'dar.  It
was a hard fought battle, no captives taken on either side.  The Via
Petrus continues west on the far side of the square.

Exits.Description:
Just east of here a large number of citizens are entering and leaving
a huge marble building.

Wonderful smells emanate from a little shop on the ground floor of an
apartment building.
via Petrus continues in the direction of the setting sun.

Rooms.Name: The Bakery
Rooms.Description:
Long golden loaves of bread rest beside delicate, rich rolls and
flat breads and crackers.  The aromas wafting from the kitchen are
making your mouth water.  The only exit is to the south.

Exits.Description:
A much smellier place, via Petrus lies just out the door to the
north.

Rooms.Name: Opening of a large meadow
Rooms.Description:
The sparse trees give way completely here to a large open meadow
filled with men of all ages dressed in mid-thigh length tunics, light
weight metal armor and carrying small round shields.  A path leads
south towards a large clay road, and to the east and west are small
stands of trees.

Exits.Description: You can see a large open field with a lot of people exercising on it.

You can see an impressively built very wide clay road stretching east
and west.

Rooms.Name: Field of Mars - SW
Rooms.Description:
The training field stretches far to the north and east of you.
During the day, the gently rolling, grass covered meadow is teeming
with soldiers running, stretching, and learning the arts of war.  To
the south lies the road to the city of Rome (where all roads lead).
To the west you can see peaceful farmland, part of some noble's
estate.

Exits.Description: All around you you see men and women exercising.
All around you you see men and women exercising.
All around you you see men and women exercising.

Rooms.Name: Field of Mars - NW
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the northwest corner of an enormous military
training field.  Roman citizens are building strong, healthy bodies
to survive the rigors of war, and being taught the arts of war.  For
these soldiers, this includes digging canals, building roads and
bridges and making camp.  To the north and west of you lies gently
rolling farmland.  This particular area is part of a noble estate.

Exits.Description: All around you you see men and women exercising.
All around you you see men and women exercising.

Rooms.Name: Field of Mars - NE
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the northeast corner of the Field of Mars,
where Romans keep fit and where the famous army is trained.  Although
originally only land-owning citizens were allowed to serve, lately
the ranks have been opened to poorer citizens and they have been
joining in large numbers.  If they survive their 20 years of service,
they will be given a small pension or a plot of land.

Exits.Description: All around you you see men and women exercising.
All around you you see men and women exercising.

Up a slight hill you see the white marble steps and graceful statues
of a small temple.

Rooms.Name: Field of Mars - SE
Rooms.Description:
As you gaze across this vast plain that the Romans call the Field
of Mars, you see large groups of men (human and otherwise) training
for the rigors of war.  Here they are lifting weights, building up
muscle mass.  They will have to carry their weapons, three days worth
of supplies and the implements for road and bridge and camp building
on their backs.  If they can't keep up, the penalties are harsh.

Exits.Description: All around you you see men and women exercising.
All around you you see men and women exercising.

Rooms.Name: Temple Steps - Venus
Rooms.Description:
You are midway up a short flight of steps leading to the temple to
the goddess Venus.  White marble columns tower above you, before a
narrow flat porch where ceremonies are held.

Exits.Description: A busy street lies north, down a short flight of steps
The shadowy cavern of an inner temple lies through a small doorway.
The Forum, center of life in Rome, is filled with activity.

Rooms.Name: Temple to Venus
Rooms.Description:
This single, large room is dedicated to the goddess of love and
beauty, Venus.  Around the sides of the room, silver sconces hold
torches which provide the meager light.  In the center of the temple
stands a statue of the goddess in all her beauty. Around the feet of
the goddess lie offerings of flowers and sweet wine.

Exits.Description: Through a narrow door you can see the steps of the temple.

Rooms.Name: The Forum - NE
Rooms.Description:
This enormous open area is the center of Roman political and civil
life.  All around you throngs of people are purchasing exotic items
from street vendors, politicians are politicking, tourists from the
provinces are gawking, and people are going about their daily lives.
The forum continues west and south from here, and a large avenue
leads east towards the East Gate.

Exits.Description: via Petrus stretches as far as your eye can see to the east.

All kinds of vendors from all over the Empire seem to have gathered
here.

A shrine to the goddess Vesta lies in the western section of the
Forum.

Rooms.Name: The Forum - SE
Rooms.Description:
This part of the forum is bordered by the western wall of the
temple of Venus and the large public building devoted to the courts
to the south.  The forum continues west and north.

Exits.Description:
Vendors, tourists, citizens busy about their business all hurry
through
the forum.
A short flight of steps leads up to the beautiful temple of Venus.
The large open square of the forum continues west.

Rooms.Name: The Forum - NW
Rooms.Description:
A small altar holds an eternal fire, tended by 6 priestesses known
as the Vestal Virgins.  The altar honors Vesta, ancient goddess of
the hearth.  The Vestals are chosen from the best Roman families, and
will serve for 30 years.  They will protect the flame with their
lives.  The Forum continues east and south of here.

Exits.Description:
A broad but busy street lies to the north, lined with buildings of
all shapes and sizes.
More Forum, with its vendors, tourists, senators and slaves ...

The large open forum continues, filled with all manner of people and
activity.

In the far distance you can see the east gate of Rome.  via Phobia
will take you there, if you dare.

Rooms.Name: The Forum - SW
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the southwest corner of a huge open area in
the heart of the city of Rome.  This is a popular meeting place, the
center of "downtown", near the important temples, public buildings
and baths.  The important shrine to the goddess Vesta is just north
of here, and via Phobia continues to the west.

Exits.Description: Just north of here in the temple you spot the priestesses of Vesta.
The beautiful temple to Venus can be seen from here, past the crowds.
via Rodentia runs past the large Theater building.

Rooms.Name: Via Rodentia
Rooms.Description:
The broad thoroughfare Via Rodentia travels north from here
towards two enormous buildings, and the road is packed tightly with
people of all classes traveling to and from the entertainments.  To
the east lies an enormous office building, the Basilica Melodia
(named for Praetor Petyus's third wife).  On the west you can see the
graceful white columns of the Temple to Vulcan.

Exits.Description:
Although you can barely see the road for all the people, it appears
well-paved and well-swept.
White marble steps rise to the temple of Vulcan.

Rooms.Name: Via Rodentia
Rooms.Description:
To both the west of you stands an enormous building dedicated to
entertainment.  The wall to the east is covered with posters showing
men and beasts in mortal combat.  The words "Colosseum - Main Entrance"
are carved in stone over an archway.  To the west, elegant marble steps
lead up to an important temple.  via Rodentia continues in a straight
path north and south.

Exits.Description: via Rodentia continues past the enormous racetrack, Circus Maximus.

From the huge building you hear cries of excitement and cries of
pain.

The center of town is filled with vendors, citizens, soldiers home on
leave from the ever expanding frontiers.

A huge statue to Mercury leads you to believe this building is one of
his many temples.

Rooms.Name: Via Rodentia
Rooms.Description:
Enormous stone buildings lie to the east and west of your spot on
this broad thoroughfare.  Both are supported by long rows of arched
columns, which bear the enormous weight of many tons of stone and
concrete.  From the west wafts the strong smell of horses, and there
is an entrance to this racetrack just under the archway labeled
"Circus Maximus" to the west.  To the east, under a sign reading
"#rGladiators Only!!#N" you see a small tunnel ending in darkness.

Exits.Description: Ahead, the North Gate appears to be well guarded and closed.
A small dark tunnel smells of fear and death.
via Rodentia will take you swiftly back to the center of town.

The pounding of hooves and the smell of horse dung lure you to the
entrance of the racetrack.

Rooms.Name: Via Rulia
Rooms.Description:
A small dark alleyway between buildings leads north to the actor's
entrance to the stage and east to a broader road.  The alley is not
paved, just hard packed dirt lies beneath your feet.

Exits.Description: Through a narrow archway you can see the theater stage.
The narrow little alley takes you to a broad thoroughfare.

Rooms.Name: Via Rulia
Rooms.Description:
This short narrow dark alley lies between the stage entrance for
the theater to the west and a broader, better lit roadway to the west.
The alley is bordered on the north and south by large brick buildings.

Exits.Description: The little alley ends on the broad via Rodentia.
The little alley ends at the actors' entrance to the theater.

Rooms.Name: Intersection of Via Rodentia and Via Rulia
Rooms.Description:
Just south of the grand public entrance to the theater lies a
small alleyway which follows along the side of the theater building.
A poor alley, it is unpaved and must be very muddy when it rains.
The walls around you are covered with posters for the current comedy
being presented at the theater.

Exits.Description: The large entryway to the Theater is just up ahead.
A huge and very well kept basilica looks open for business.
Through the South Gate of Rome you can see rolling hills.

A small dark alleyway leads to what looks like a small side entrance
into the theater.

Rooms.Name: Stage Left
Rooms.Description:
A large groove at the front of the stage holds the curtain,
brought up for scene changes and at the beginning and end of the
plays in this theater.  Behind you, complex machinery raises and
lowers the elaborate scenery.  Stage Right is north of here, and you
can explore the backstage to the west, or leave the stage area
through the door on the south.

Exits.Description: The stage continues north of you.
Through an archway you can see a little alleyway.
The backstage area is scary ... filled with all kinds of props!

Rooms.Name: Stage Right
Rooms.Description:
Don't look up!  High over your head the superstructure is crammed
with machinery designed to hold gods swinging through the background
of melodramas and lower heavy scenery onto the stage.  Below you a
trap door provides access for monsters and ghouls to erupt from Hell
amidst clouds of smoke and fire.

Exits.Description: The stage continues south of you.
The backstage area is scary ... filled with all kinds of props!

Rooms.Name: Front Row Seats
Rooms.Description:
This row of seats provides the best view in the house of the
stage.  It is reserved for Senators, Consuls, the Praetor and other
nobility, all of whom contribute heavily to the upkeep of the
theater.

Exits.Description:
You can see some of your friends sitting just to your right as you face
the stage.
The hoi polloi sits behind you.  Ignore them.

The stage production is pretty wild, with actors popping up from
beneath the floor, sets dropping down from the ceiling ...
The cheaper seats and noisier crowd ...

Rooms.Name: Senator's Seating
Rooms.Description:
Seated right in front of the stage, you feel a part of every
production.  Unfortunately, sometimes Caesar likes to take the stage,
and then there is no escaping unnoticed.

Exits.Description: Some of your friends are sitting to your left.
A few steps up, the poorer citizens and freedmen sit.

Rooms.Name: Middle Tier Seating - South
Rooms.Description:
Stone hard benches (made of stone) form rows leading up from the
stage.  In your grandfathers' day, people stood to watch the plays,
but a generous citizen (who wanted to achieve great political
office!) donated this new theater with seating.

Exits.Description: Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.

Rooms.Name: Middle Tier Seating - Center
Rooms.Description:
You are right in the middle of the theater.  You are center stage
and halfway between the nobles (ahead of you) and poorer Romans
(higher up). The play is a farce you have seen many times before.

Exits.Description: Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.

Rooms.Name: Middle Tier Seating - North
Rooms.Description:
The theater is fairly enormous, but as Rome's population has
swollen with not only citizens and slaves but merchants and traders
and travelers, the theater seats are often crowded.  Rome has become
quite wealthy from it's conquests, and the business of entertainment
has become quite lucrative.

Exits.Description: Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.

Rooms.Name: Cheap Seats - By the wall
Rooms.Description:
One of the worst places to sit, high up with the women and slaves
and the otherwise disenfranchised of Rome.  Still, the excellent
engineering of this theater means you can hear every word of the
silly farce.

Exits.Description: Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.

A small set of stairs begins under a dark red, strangely glowing sign
that reads "#RExit#N".
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.

Rooms.Name: Cheap Seats - South Center
Rooms.Description:
No togas up here.  These benches are for the lower class and
poorest of Romans.  Still, since there are public baths available to
everybody, your nose isn't distracting you TOO much from the play.

Exits.Description: Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.

Rooms.Name: Cheap Seats - North Center
Rooms.Description:
Dead center above the stage, which is far, far below you.  You
could probably hear the actors if it weren't for all the noise from
the rabble around you.  This theater was built by Pompey and holds
about 27,000 people.  It's pretty crowded today!

Exits.Description: Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.

Rooms.Name: Cheap seats - By the stairs
Rooms.Description:
Fortunately today's play is pretty simple.  You recognize all the
familiar roles by the masks the actors wear.  A fight has broken out
between two groups of spectators to one side of you, and on the
other, a group has started throwing things at the actors.  Guess they
don't like the play!

Exits.Description: Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.

Rooms.Name: Stairs to Entrance
Rooms.Description:
A long dark winding set of stairs leads to the grand entrance to
the theater.  To the south and west you see a vast semicircular sea
of stone benches packed with a rowdy crowd out for a good time.

Exits.Description: Wherever you look, you see more hard benches.
Long dark winding stairs will take you to the grand entrance.

Rooms.Name: Bottom of the Stairs
Rooms.Description:
A long, gracefully winding staircase leads up to the cheaper
seats.  The stairs are lit by an occasional torch, but are otherwise
quite dark.

Exits.Description:
The Theater Lobby is crowded with people buying tickets to see
tonight's
plays.
Noise of a rowdy crowd drifts down through the stairwell.

Rooms.Name: Theater Entrance
Rooms.Description:
The huge entrance lobby is lavishly decorated with murals showing
scenes from the the theater's most popular plays.  Some of the
riffraff loiters here, hoping to catch a glimpse of their favorite
actors, but the actors actually have their own entrance down an
alleyway south of here.

Exits.Description:
The busy thoroughfare via Rodentia catches your attention to the
east.

Rooms.Name: via Rodentia
Rooms.Description:
via Rodentia is a straight street running north-south from the
south gate of Rome to the Forum, at the center of town, then north
again to the north gate.  It is one of the two main streets of Rome,
and as such is lined with important buildings such as the enormous
theater to the west and the office building (basilica) to the east.
The offices appear closed, but you may enter the theater.

Exits.Description: The lovely via Rodentia continues.

A broad path leads east from via Rodentia past large buildings towards
the east wall of Rome.

via Rodentia intersects with a small alleyway just south of here,
before reaching the grand South Gate.
A crowd of people is entering the graceful building to the west.

Rooms.Name: via Rodentia
Rooms.Description:
You are traveling along via Rodentia, south of the center of town
(the Forum).  To the west lie the arched walls of the huge theater
complex recently built.  The entrance is south of here.  The street
on the east is blocked by a huge office building.  The street itself
runs north and south.

Exits.Description: Looking north you can see the huge open square the marks the Forum.
Just south of here is the huge theater built by Pompey.

Rooms.Name: Backstage
Rooms.Description:
Behind the scenery you can see the marvelous machinery that makes
a visit to the theater here so exciting.  Great piles of props are
lying around, waiting for plays by Plautus and Terence or dramas
translated from the Greek by Livius Andronicus.  The theater is
competing for patronage with the spectacles at the Colosseum and the
races at the circus, so the plays are getting more and more
outrageous.

Exits.Description: The front of the stage is just east of here.
Climb over some props and you'll be onstage!

Rooms.Name: Circus Maximus - Entrance
Rooms.Description:
A break in the long series of columns reveals the entrance to
Circus Maximus!  Posters announce the races for today - an exciting
series of 24 races between Rome's favorite teams.  You know they are
Rome's favorites by the graffiti which you've seen all along the
outside walls of this huge arena.  The ticket booth is here.

Exits.Description:
Looking east you can see people headed out of and into the city as
well as joining you at the racetrack.

Rooms.Name: Waiting Area:  North
Rooms.Description:
This large, crowded area lies directly under the spectators' main
entrance.  Chariots and the freedmen and slaves who maintain them and
drive them mill about, waiting for their race to begin.  The area
continues to the south.  The exit to the street is north.

Exits.Description: The broad avenue via Artemis runs east and west.

Horses and chariots await the call for their race, moving about
restlessly.

Rooms.Name: Waiting Area:  South
Rooms.Description:
A large, noisy, crowded area is filled with charioteers
impatiently waiting their turn to race around the track for the glory
of their team (and a lot of gold).  Some of them have won great fame
and riches successfully racing.  Some may find themselves on the
gladiatorial fields if they do not win.  The entrance to the race is
west.

Exits.Description:
The thunder of horses and a massive cloud of dust rises from the
racetrack.

Rooms.Name: The track: Start!
Rooms.Description:
The praetor has dropped the white flag, and the chariots are off
and racing!  It was very foolish of you to wander onto the track, for
only winning matters to these teams and you are likely to be
trampled.

Exits.Description: You have no choice but to follow the horses around the track!

Rooms.Name: The track:  And they're off!
Rooms.Description:
You must hurry east around the thick spina running down the center
of the track.  The ground is soft beneath your feet, marked with the
hooves of the racing horses and the wheel tracks from the chariots.

Exits.Description: You can't see much but a cloud of dust and the back end of a horse.

Rooms.Name: The track: At the turn
Rooms.Description:
The chariots race as close to the central barrier as they dare
here.  They must balance the risks of tipping over their chariot (and
being killed by closely following horses) with losing time taking a
slightly longer route further from the edge.

Exits.Description: More dust, more chariots, more horses!

Rooms.Name: The track:  On the final lap
Rooms.Description:
The many tiers of the circus surround you here, rising high.
Rabid fans will make successful charioteers wealthy men, and the
losers ... may find themselves with another career.  The home stretch
is west.

Exits.Description:
You can't see anything but you can hear the thunder of hooves behind
you.

Rooms.Name: The track:  Home stretch
Rooms.Description:
The tall central spine of the track looms north of you, a grand
wall dividing the track into a large, narrow oval.  Atop the wall a
freedman counts laps for the spectators.  At the moment he is
excitedly waving his arms at you.  Is it because you are in danger?
or just interfering with the races?

Exits.Description: A great cloud of dust obscures the finish line ahead.

Rooms.Name: The track:  Safety ahead
Rooms.Description:
The loop of racetrack ends just west of here, although the
chariots may head south for another lap.  The citizens take their
entertainments seriously, though, and I wouldn't interfere with it if
I were you!

Exits.Description: A massive cloud of dust obscures all views.
A massive cloud of dust obscures all views.

Rooms.Name: Chariot Drivers' Entrance
Rooms.Description:
Just to the east of here the busy via Rodentia leads to the north
gate of Rome.  This street runs between the north wall and the side
of a huge building.  You can tell by the cheers and the pounding of
hooves and the track of horse dung along the street that this must be
the racetrack, Circus Maximus.

Exits.Description: The street intersects ahead with via Rodentia.
Charioteers and horses enter the huge building through this entrance.

Rooms.Name: Entrance to Racetrack Seating - South
Rooms.Description:
Crowds of Romans pour into the seating area of the circus.  Horse
and chariot racing are great entertainment for all levels of Roman
society.  There's always the chance one of the charioteers will be
trampled or crushed as he goes around the bend, and of course you
have to yell for your team.

Exits.Description:
The entrance to the seating area continues, a bare room of white
stone covered with a layer of dust from the racetrack.
Lavishly dressed men in togas fill the stone benches to the west.
Broad steps lead up to cheaper seats.

Rooms.Name: Entrance to Racetrack Seating - North
Rooms.Description:
The nobles and senators seats begin their circle around the
racetrack just west of here, and there are stairs up to the plebeian
seats, further up to the cheap seats, or you can head down to the
street.  But why do that when you have just bought your ticket?

Exits.Description: The large anteroom continues south to more stairs and seating.
A row of white togas tells you this is citizen only seating.
Stairs lead steeply up to cheaper seats.
You can reach the street via a set of stone steps leading down.

Rooms.Name: Augustus Maximus
Rooms.Description:
You have quite bravely entered the box of Augustus Aurelius
Maximus himself.  As you might guess from his deep green tunic,
Augustus is the primary supporter of the green team.  Augustus and
his friends frequently avail themselves of this box to watch and
wager on the races.  The box leads west to other nobles' boxes, or
east to the Circus'
entrance.

Exits.Description: The main entrance to this area lies east of here through an archway.
Augustus' cousin Julius has his seat off to the west.

Rooms.Name: Julius Maximus
Rooms.Description:
This box is usually used by the famous senator Julius Homerus
Maximus.  He backs the green team, one of the most popular of the
Roman chariot teams.  He found their lead charioteer, Jose, when he
was acting as proconsul in Spain.  If this team does not win, there may
be riots in the streets. There are more boxes to the east and west, but
you can have a good view of the races from here.

Exits.Description: Brother Augustus has his box just east of you.
Brother Gluteus and his entourage are just to your left.

Rooms.Name: Gluteus Maximus
Rooms.Description:
Soft cushions laid on top of hard stone benches cushion the
tender bottoms of Gluteus' friends and family.  From the crumbs
remaining on the flooring here you can see he enjoys his food very
well!  You are so close to the racetrack you can nearly touch the
horses as they fly past north of you.  Praetor Petyus's box is in the
honored position to your left, your cousin Julius's box is to your
right.

Exits.Description: A stretch of stone seats designated for the senators.
The rich appointments tell you this must be the box of the Praetor.
A broad set of steps leads up to cheaper seats.

Rooms.Name: The Praetor's Box
Rooms.Description:
The head of state for Rome has his own box here.  A wily politician,
he is seen to support the popular green team.  From here he can easily
see (and be seen by) the entire circus.  Boxes belonging to nobles lie
north-east and southeast of here.  To the immediate south lie some
steps to reach the upper levels.

Exits.Description: More of the Praetors friends are just north of here.

Gluteus Maximus has this set of well padded benches to the
southeast.
Narrow steps lead up to cheaper seats.

Rooms.Name: A Noble's Box South of the Praetor's Stand
Rooms.Description:
You are in the box of a noble at one end of the long raceway.
This is a wild and busy day at the circus, with 250,000 wildly
enthusiastic racing fans cheering on their favorite.  Judging by the
blue colors you see here, this noble favors the conservative party's
team, the Blues (the Venetians).  The praetor's box is just north of
here, and other nobles boxes lie to the west.  To the east there are
some steps leading up to the plebeians and lower-status boxes.

Exits.Description: The nobles' seating continues.
Praetor Petyus is watching you! Watch out!
A steep flight of stone steps leads up.

Rooms.Name: Marcus Wallgrenus Boxus
Rooms.Description:
The famous Roman legal eagle Marcus Wallgrenus brings important
clients here to entertain them with an afternoon at the raceway.  From
here they have a clear view of the horses, who pound by almost within
touching distance of them.  The citizens' seats continue east and west.

Exits.Description:
Off to your left, more of your friends and fellow citizens cheer on
the politically correct teams.
Is the Praetor watching you?

Rooms.Name: Seating for Citizens
Rooms.Description:
A cloud of dust, the crack of whips and pounding of hooves and the
group of small chariots fly by you.  It's a do-or-die race for the
charioteers, who hope to win fame and fortune in the race.  For the
nobles it's a chance to be seen at a popular sport rooting for the
right  side.  Seating continues west, and the main entrance lies off
to the east.  Climbing up these steps will take you to the cheaper
seats.

Exits.Description: Through the arch you can see people hurrying to their seats.

To your right your friends and fellow citizens cheer on the
politically correct teams.
A narrow flight of stone steps leads up.

Rooms.Name: Plebeian Seats
Rooms.Description:
The hard concrete benches don't affect the enthusiasm of the
racing fans here.  These seats are usually packed with Rome's
second-class citizens, the plebeians, cheering wildly for the Leeks
(the green team) or the Venetians (the blue team).  You will see a
lot of gold changing hands as people bet on their favorite team.

Exits.Description: More stone benches lie to your east, packed with Romans.
The wall of the two story Praetor's box lies west of you.
Narrow stone steps lead up to the cheap seats.
Narrow stone steps lead down to the citizens' seats.

Rooms.Name: Plebeian Seats
Rooms.Description:
The wealthy but not-quite-noble sit in these seats, cheering on
the leeks, their favorite team.  These are the shop owners, freedmen,
sons born of slaves or slaves who have bought their freedom.  More
plebeian seats stretch east and west of here.

Exits.Description: Long straight lines of stone benches stretch both east and west.
Long straight lines of stone benches stretch both east and west.

Rooms.Name: Plebeian Seats
Rooms.Description:
The hard stone seats stretch endlessly west from here.  Vendors
wander up and down, selling refreshments so that spectators need
never leave their seats.  Far to the west and down you can see the
elaborately columned box of the Praetor.

Exits.Description: A dark door is marked with the single word "#rExit#N" (glowing).
The circus stretches west for over 550m (1800ft).
Cheaper seats lie up the narrow stone steps.
The citizens' seats (and the exit) are down this flight of steps.

Rooms.Name: Plebeian Seats - South Side
Rooms.Description:
Across the wide (180m / 600ft) racetrack you can see a vast sea of
faces on all three levels of the circus.  You can push your way
through the crowd east from here, or look for more seats up or down
the narrow stone steps.

Exits.Description: More crowded seats!
A dark door is marked with the single word "#rExit#N" (glowing).
Narrow stone steps lead up to more seats.
Narrow stone steps lead down to more seats.

Rooms.Name: Plebeian Seats - South Side
Rooms.Description:
If today's races don't come out as hoped, there may be a riot here
at the Circus.  The racetrack is crowded in both directions - east
and west, and you worry about being trampled if the wrong team wins.
Or if the right one does.

Exits.Description: A large excited crowd sits and stands on long rows of stone benches.
A large excited crowd sits and stands on long rows of stone benches.

Rooms.Name: Plebeian Seats - South Side
Rooms.Description:
The heat of the day combined with the sweaty bodies of 250,000
spectators at today's race and the wild excitement is enough to make
anyone just a bit nauseous.  You can head down the short flight of
steps to the exit, or up the same flight to sit under the slight
awning at the back of the top tier of the circus.

Exits.Description: More seats!  More spectators!
Up the narrow steps lie the cheapest seats.
Down the narrow steps lies the way out of the circus.

Rooms.Name: The Third Tier
Rooms.Description:
Stairs leading down to the plebeians and nobles' sections lie at
your right hand as you watch the race in front of you.  This section
is reserved for slaves and women.  To the west there is a seemingly
endless stretch of benches.  The circus can and often does seat
250,000 screaming Romans.

Exits.Description: A sea of seats north and south of here.
A sea of seats north and south of here.
Narrow stone steps lead down.

Rooms.Name: The Third Tier
Rooms.Description:
The cleaning crew clearly hasn't made it up here for a long time.
You are w-a-a-a-y above the racetrack.  At your back is the eastern
wall of the enormous circus, to both your left and right are more
seats, and if you wish to leave the steps down are right at your
feet.

Exits.Description: The cheap seats continue.
A dark door is marked with the single word "#rExit#N" (glowing).

You see someone who looks an AWFULLY like your cousin Homerus, the
one who spits when he talks.

The steps look too steep to negotiate safely unless you are quite
sober.

Rooms.Name: The Third Tier
Rooms.Description:
You lean back against the eastern wall of the circus and hope not
to be trampled by all the race goers.   The crowds are truly amazing.
The races really pack 'em in, even more than the gladiators over at
the Colosseum or the plays in the theater.

Exits.Description: A dark door is marked with the single word "#rExit#N" (glowing).
A sea of seats.
The mass of racing fans doesn't get any thinner.  Nor do the fans.
A narrow flight of stone steps leads down.

Rooms.Name: The Third Tier
Rooms.Description:
This is where many of the common Roman citizens are seated during
the games.  Like the other commoners' areas in the coliseum, it could
use extensive renovation and cleaning. This area extends to the north
and lots of noise can be heard coming from the south.

Exits.Description: A rowdy crowd over thataway.
A rowdy crowd thisaway.
Narrow steps lead down to more elegant seating.

Rooms.Name: The Third Tier
Rooms.Description:
Facing the distant racetrack, down many levels from here, the
northernmost wall of the circus is to your back, and vast numbers of
stone benches stretch to your right and left.  The wall continues up
high above your head.

Exits.Description: More seats! More excited fans!
More seats! More excited fans!
A dark door is marked with the single word "#rExit#N" (glowing).
Narrow stone steps lead down to more seats.

Rooms.Name: The Third Tier
Rooms.Description:
With your back to the wall, you enjoy the feel of the cool stone
and the small awning overhead that provides some shade.  While it's
not the best view of the racetrack far below, it may be one of the
more comfortable seats!

Exits.Description: More crowds, more seats.
More crowds, more seats.
Narrow stone steps lead down to more seats.

Rooms.Name: The Third Tier
Rooms.Description:
This is where many of the common Roman citizens are seated during
the games.  These are the cheapest seats in the house, as glare from
the sun is usually a problem during the afternoon. Like the other
common seating  areas, this place could stand extensive renovation
and a thorough cleaning. This area extends to the north and east and
a much more elegant seating area can be seen below.

Exits.Description: The crowd is just as rowdy to the north.
The crowd is just as rowdy to the east.
Down some narrow stone steps is a rowdy crowd.

Rooms.Name: The Third Tier
Rooms.Description:
Stairs leading down to the rows of the more privileged and
prosperous are on your right as you watch the races, and long rows of
concrete benches stretch to the west.  You can take the stairs down a
level if you dare, or watch the races from here.  West of the stairs
lies the wall of the Praetor's box.

Exits.Description: More seats lie beyond the steps.
More seats and more crowds
Narrow stone steps lead down to better seats.

Rooms.Name: A Dusty Old Shop
Rooms.Description:
Odd artifacts from the far reaches of the empire line the dusty
shelves of this small shop.  The proprietor is nowhere in evidence,
but you don't wonder at this, for there seems little here that anyone
would want to steal, let alone buy!  A dusty curtain hangs across the
back wall.

Exits.Description: The busy via Petrus is just north of here.
A dusty curtain conceals ... what?

Rooms.Name: Behind the Dusty Curtain
Rooms.Description:
Some sort of alchemical research is apparently the purpose for this
room.  Jars of odd colors have contents that seems even more odd.
Smoke rises slowly in an odd swirl from a pink glass pot sitting on
the low table in the middle of the room.

Exits.Description: Through the dusty curtain you see a dim little shop.

Rooms.Name: The South Gate
Rooms.Description:
This is the southern gateway to the city of Rome. The bronze gate
is closed but not locked. Looking through the bars, you see a heavily
traveled road leading out of the city. The grand new amphitheater is
just north west of here.

Exits.Description: via Rodentia runs straight north to the Forum.
A well paved road leads south through rolling farmland.

Rooms.Name: The Great North Gate
Rooms.Description:
This is the northern gateway to the city of Rome. The huge gate
appears to be closed and locked against intrusion. A large road muddy
road runs through the gate and into the countryside. via Rodentia
runs south from here.

Exits.Description:
via Rodentia runs straight to the Forum, past banks and huge
buildings dedicated to entertainments.

To the west you notice chariots and horses and small wiry men entering
and leaving the building.

A number of horses and racing chariots appear to be entering the circus
through a large archway just west of here.

Rooms.Name: via Petrus
Rooms.Description:
Via Petrus continues between the commemorative arch and the Forum.
This wide main street leads straight from the east gate at one end of
the city, through the central square, the Forum, and out the west
gate.  It is intersected at several points by other streets both broad
and narrow, and is lined with important-looking buildings.

Exits.Description: The street runs east through the Triumphal Arch.
Graceful columns lead into a white marble temple.

A broad open square is filled with people and lined with important
buildings.

Rooms.Name: Temple of Mars
Rooms.Description:
A short flight of white marble steps leads up to the temple to the
god of war, Mars.  There is a large shaded porch here where most of
the ceremonies take place.  The temple is lavishly decorated with
ornate columns and there is evidence of recent sacrifices to the god.
Perhaps the Roman army is once again on the march.

Exits.Description: A set of doors twice the height of a man open into the inner sanctum.

Down a short flight of stairs you can see a large grassy field with
many men and women exercising.

Rooms.Name: Temple of Mars
Rooms.Description:
The temple is dominated by an enormous statue of the god Mars.
Smooth muscles show the Roman ideal of manhood.  He is surrounded by
treasures won in his name or donated by citizens in his honor.  The 
many priests at the temple will guard the treasure.

Exits.Description: The porch to the temple lies south of here.

Rooms.Name: Stairs
Rooms.Description:
Wide stone steps lead up to the upper stories of this building.
Some graffiti mars the stucco walls, but the steps are clean.  From
the slight indentations in the stone you can tell that the steps are
well-used.  North of here you can see the busy via Petrus.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: #w    Go #GLeeks!!!#N

Rooms.Name: via Dulcia
Rooms.Description:
A small narrow pathway fits tightly between a large block of
apartments and small shops and the eastern wall of the city. Rome has
grown rapidly, thanks to its many conquests.  The little alley is
busy with merchants and citizens, slaves and women all busy going
somewhere.  The eastern gate of the city is just north of here, a
small shop with a tantalizing smell is just west, the eastern wall
of the city is to the east, and the street continues south.

Exits.Description:
The grand gates of Rome lie just north, with a large number of people
passing through in both directions.
The small dim alley continues south, where it meets via Vestia
Smells of sizzling meat waft out the open door of this hot food shop.

Rooms.Name: via Vestia
Rooms.Description:
via Dulcia meets via Vestia at the corner of this large building
with shops on the ground floor.  To the north, at the northern end of
this building you can see the eastern gate of Rome and the eastern
wall frames via Dulcia in that direction.  To the west you see an
endless sea of buildings and temples, typical of a big city.  The
path south is blocked by a large building and to the immediate west
there is yet another small shop, the first along via Vestia

Exits.Description: A small, narrow walkway leads north to the East Gate.

via Vestia continues past many small shops towards a tall elegant
marble building.

Rooms.Name: Hot Food
Rooms.Description:
Delicious roast meat smells lure you in to this small hot-food
store.  You fight with a mass of Roman slaves for your place in line.
Surely this is an indication that the food to be had here is as good as
it smells!  The only exit you see is to the east, back to the street.

Exits.Description: The little walkway, via Dulcia, lies just outside the shop door.

Rooms.Name: via Vestia by the Image Works
Rooms.Description:
A broad path, busy with foot traffic and, after dark, small carts,
via Vestia winds past busy little shops and small parks between the
eastern wall of Rome and the theater you see in the far distance to
the west.  Immediately north of you lies a small shop that looks
rather interesting.

Exits.Description:
Interesting smells and sights through this doorway ... You see a
small sign saying "Image Works".

via Vestia ends just east of here, where it meets via Dulcia and the
eastern wall of Rome.
via Vestia continues towards a small group of very large buildings.

Rooms.Name: Image Works
Rooms.Description:
Appearances may be deceiving, but appearance is important!  This
small shop sells the necessities for keeping you looking like a
citizen on the move up!  It is a small room lined with shelves which
are, in turn, lined with jars of cosmetics and depilatories.  A pair of
slaves has been set up in this shop by one of the wealthier Romans.
They will soon be able to buy their freedom.  In the meantime they are
making a tidy fortune from the vanity of their fellow Romans.

Exits.Description: via Vestia lies right out the door.

Rooms.Name: via Vestia by the Fuller
Rooms.Description:
This broad path gets a lot of traffic, leading as it does past
shops and apartments, theaters and courts.  Just to the north on this
part of the street lies the fuller's shop.  via Vestia continues east
and west from here.

Exits.Description:
Strong smells and a wave of heat flow from the small fuller's shop
north of here.
Not far from here via Vestia runs into the Eastern Wall of the city.
A strongly unpleasant odor comes to you from the south.
Off in the distance there is a small cluster of large buildings.

Rooms.Name: A Fuller
Rooms.Description:
Keeping your toga white in a society that has yet to discover soap
requires some doing.  The fuller is here to help you.  Using a
special kind of clay known as "fuller's earth", many stains can be
removed and you can once again wear clothes as sweet smelling as your
body!  Fortunately for toga wearers, one size fits all.

Exits.Description: via Phobia beckons to you from the open doorway.

Rooms.Name: Jewelry Shop
Rooms.Description:
Beautiful rings, bracelets and cameos, necklaces and waist chains
all glitter from the tables of this very exclusive little shops.
Beautiful jewels from the far reaches of the republic have been
brought here and fashioned into beautiful ornaments for the wealthy.
The street lies south, past the burly guards.

Exits.Description: The busy street is just outside the door.

Rooms.Name: via Vestia outside the Jewelry Shop
Rooms.Description:
This part of the street tends to be a bit crowded as there are
usually strong guards by the Jeweler's' to the north.  It is a small
shop, well kept.  The street continues east and west from here.

Exits.Description: A tiny jewel of a shop lies just north of here.

Off to the east in the distance you can see the great rise of the
East Wall.
Not so far off lies the theater!

Rooms.Name: via Vestia
Rooms.Description:
You are surrounded by the large buildings and rapid pace of a
large city.  Just south of you lies a large white marble building, at
least two stories tall.  Directly to the west is the graceful theater
building, and the path north on via Phobia leads past several shops
to a lovely small temple devoted to Venus.

Exits.Description:
via Phobia runs the short distance along the length of the building
just to the east to the via Petrus.
via Vestia continues eastward to the eastern wall of Rome.
The steps of the great court building are just south of here.

The intersection of via Vestia with via Rodentia is a busy one.
Directly across the busy street lies the theater!

Rooms.Name: Swords 'R  Us
Rooms.Description:
Welcome to the weapon shop of Titus Andronicus!! Rare halberds,
whips, swords and other instruments of death are proudly displayed on
the walls and in gleaming glass cases. More common weapons are
stacked like wood on the floor.

Exits.Description: You can spot some armor in this direction.

Across a short but busy street you can hear what sounds like a very wild
party.

Rooms.Name: via Artemis
Rooms.Description:
This little road runs north and south between via Vestia and
via Petrus, past small shops and temples.  Just east of here lies a
small armory.  To the north you see the back of the temple to Venus,
just west lies the temple to Bacchus (from which you hear a great
deal of noise) and the via Vestia, a broad road, lies directly to the
south.

Exits.Description:
The smell of leather, bronze and steel comes to you from the shop
just east of here.
via Vestia
Loud sounds of parties and play come from the temple to the west.

Rooms.Name: Good as New Armor
Rooms.Description:
Good equipment is important for soldiers of the republic!  And
with the ... er ... short lifespan of the gladiators, there seems to
always be (slightly used) equipment available for sale here.  There
IS a slight remaining smell of blood and sweat here that just won't
quite come out of even some of the best pieces.  The street is right
out the door to the west.

Exits.Description: Look sharp!

Rooms.Name: Wild and Crazy
Rooms.Description:
Up a short flight of steps, on a wide portico a celebration is
going on.  Grapes from the last harvest and wine from the good years
before that are brought in offering to the god of wine and fertility.
Inside the temple (west from here) you hear moans and soft murmurs of
what sounds like a group of Romans having an outrageously good time.
Not in the mood to party?  The street is still just east of here.

Exits.Description: A quiet little paved street is just east of here.
Hmm ...

Rooms.Name: Bacchus
Rooms.Description:
Bacchanalia, celebrations of wine, song and fertility, take place
here on a regular basis.  Anything to keep the gods appeased.  The
Romans will make that sacrifice! The party continues on the temple's
portico east of here.

Exits.Description: Sounds of a party ... perhaps you should go see.

Rooms.Name: Courts - Grand Central Hallway
Rooms.Description:
Gleaming black and white marble squares make a formal pattern in
floor of this grand hallway.  You are in the central hallway of one
of the huge basilicas in Rome, an office building filled with courts
and law offices and business offices of all sizes.  There are lovely
archways both north and south, and the Grand Hallway continues east.
Sounds of street traffic echo vaguely from the west.

Exits.Description: Through the archway you see an elegantly furnished office.
Light gleams off of highly polished marble floors.
An ornate arch appears to lead to an office of some sort.

The grand entranceway to the basilica features a porch and many steps
down to the street.

Rooms.Name: A Statue of Jason
Rooms.Description:
You stand in the middle of a magnificent hallway, lined with white
marble columns that stretch gracefully high above you.  In the center of
the hallway is a statue of the architect's hero, Jason of the Greek
Argonaut myth.  To the west the hallway continues, ending in the street
via Rodentia.

Exits.Description:
The hallway is lined with offices and courts.  One of them is just
north of here, another to the south.
The black and white marble squares continue east and west.

The hallway is lined with offices and courts.  One of them is just
north of here, another to the south.
The black and white marble squares continue east and west.

Rooms.Name: Grand Central Hallway
Rooms.Description:
You are standing at one end of a huge open central atrium in a
large office building in Rome.  The ceiling soars two very tall
stories above you, this end capped in a half dome.  Black and white
marble squares stretch in dizzying array all the way to the entrance
at the western end.  Just north of here lies one of many Roman
courts.  To the south is a holding area.

Exits.Description:
A grand courtroom lies just north of here.  You hope the judge is in
a good mood!
A waiting room lies just to the south of here.
The beautiful lobby continues west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A marble statue of a young man in his prime, Jason bears navigational
instruments in one hand.  His attention is very focused, and you suppose
he must be concentrated on the dragon he soon will face.  He is
surrounded by statues in niches set along the sides of the hallway.
Each niche contains a statue to one of his companions on the voyage.
You can see Hercules, Castor, Pollux, Orpheus and Theseus.

Rooms.Name: Courts - Law Office of Marcus Wallgrenus
Rooms.Description:
A massive polished ebony desk greets you as you walk into this
luxuriously appointed office.  One wall is covered with shelves and
small caskets holding scrolls.  A small scribe's desk sits to one side
of the room, and two bronze and leather chairs invite you to sit while
you consult with the lawyer, Marcus Wallgrenus.  The elegant archway
south of here leads to the grand hallway of the basilica.

Rooms.Name: The Banker
Rooms.Description:
A large citizen in a pristine toga named Albertus Tellus Maximus
will handle your monetary transactions for you.  The bank is large and
luxuriously appointed with fine paintings and sculptures of gods of
wealth and power.  You can feel confident that the banker will take
good care of your money.

Exits.Description: The huge graceful lobby of the basilica lies to the south.

Rooms.Name: Courtroom
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the courtroom where citizens bring their civil
and criminal complaints.  Attached to the broad front panel of the
judge's desk you see the great seal of the republic.  The courtroom
exits to the south, but there may be another exit for the judge.

Exits.Description: An elegant archway leads to the central lobby of the building.

Rooms.Name: Waiting Area
Rooms.Description:
This beautiful space shows signs of a recent struggle.  This is
where the defendants await their trial, guarded by minions of their
accuser.  There are no state police, although there is a set of laws
created by the senate and assembly.  If you want to bring a wrongdoer
to justice, you will have to bring him there yourself!  The door to a
very grand hallway lies to the north.

Exits.Description:
The grand hallway is crowded with citizens going about their business.
Directly across the hall you see the entrance to the courtroom.

Rooms.Name: Investment Advice
Rooms.Description:
An aura of tasteful wealth fills this room, the office of one
Antonius Banderus (Quaestor Tony, Financial Advisor).  The seats
are made of an exotic leather.  From the spots you think it might be
leopard.  The walls are covered with beautiful murals depicting "the
good life".  Antonius will, for a small fee, take your money and invest
it so that you, to, may partake of the good life.  There is an archway
north leading to a very grand hallway.

Rooms.Name: Law Offices
Rooms.Description:
The law offices of Antonius the Younger are tastefully decorated
with a floor mosaic in aqua and ochre, an abstract design.  The walls
are covered with murals depicting scenes from the life of Jupiter, and
a small marble statue of Antonius the Elder sits on a pedestal in the
corner, well dusted.

Exits.Description: A beautiful Grand Hallway links all of the expensive offices.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Entrance - Patrons
Rooms.Description:
The grand entrance to the Colosseum is occupied by a small serious
man who will take your gold and sell you a ticket.  The entrance is
lit by daylight streaming in, and while you are waiting you read the
posters advertising the day's events.  After you buy your ticket, you
may activate the entrance, then enter the Colosseum.

Exits.Description: The busy street is just to the west.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Entrance - Gladiators Only
Rooms.Description:
A small dark tunnel leads to the arena itself.  This is the
gladiators' entrance, and the exit for those who are successful in
the games.  Those who do not succeed are fed to the animals.  There is
no exit from the arena without combat.  Curiosity seekers are eaten.
The arena lies to the east, the exit to the street is west.  Choose
wisely.  #wIf you are not at least level 20, you will probably die in
here.#N

Exits.Description: Can't see much of anything at the end of the tunnel.
A wiser decision!

Rooms.Name: Martyrs
Rooms.Description:
A number of martyrs have been placed here, waiting to be
executed.  It is a pitiful little room with a dirt floor, badly torn
up in places.  Some of the martyrs sit around dejectedly, waiting
to die.  Others stride about the room, glaring at nobody in
particular.  The exit, if the door hasn't closed behind you, is to
the east.

Exits.Description:
A small wooden door lies between you and the questionable safety of
the arena.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Floor - NW
Rooms.Description:
The blood-colored sands shift beneath your feet, your footing is
consequently insecure.  All around you are small doors, mostly
unmarked. With your back to the corner, the arena stretches out to both
your left and right, and the Colosseum seating rises up to the
heavens.  Neither the gods, the spectators nor the other gladiators are
likely to have mercy on you.

Exits.Description: A small nondescript wooden door appears to blend into the wall.
The bloody sand continues.
The arena stretches out to the far wall.
A small nondescript wooden door appears to be built into the wall.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Floor - NE
Rooms.Description:
What are you DOING out here?  You have a death wish or something?
This is the arena, the area where to-the-death battles take place.
You are surrounded by a vast seating area filled with Romans waiting to
watch you die.  They prefer slow and horrible, so perhaps you should
find your way out of here quickly!  The arena continues to the west
and south, and there are small doors to the north and east.

Exits.Description: A small wooden door is set into the wall.
A small wooden door is set into the wall.
The bloody arena continues south.
The bloody arena continues west.

Rooms.Name: Bear Pit
Rooms.Description:
A small tomb-like room has been set aside for the bears.  It is
clear that they are NOT happy here despite the darkness that must
remind them of winter caves.  The metal door and the walls are covered
with claw marks.  The only exit seems to be through that door to the
south.  The one that seems to be missing a doorknob.

Exits.Description: A small wooden door leads into the arena.

Rooms.Name: Wolves
Rooms.Description:
This area is where the wolves are kept prior to being unleashed to
fight other animal or human gladiators.  It is a dark and airless
place, your feeble light barely displaces the darkness.  You can feel
the distress of the animals kept here.  It lingers in the air long
after they've been set loose to prowl the arena.

Exits.Description:
A small wooden door leads into the arena.  There is no knob on this
side.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Floor - SW
Rooms.Description:
Large vats of incense sit in this and every corner of this round
arena.  The heavy perfume will perhaps disguise the smell of blood
and death that surrounds you.  The arena continues north and east, and
at your back you see two small doors.

Exits.Description: The bloody arena continues.
Smoke rises in a lazy spiral from a vat of incense.

The wall of the arena shows marks of being caught in the combat, but
you can still make out the outlines of a door.

The wall of the arena shows evidence of the many battles that have been
waged here.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Floor - SE
Rooms.Description:
The southeast wall of the arena curves around you, high over your
head.  There is no convenient rail to jump over should you suddenly
be threatened with goring by some minotaur.  Over your head, the a
mosaic spells out your grand entrance words, "We who are about to die
salute you!!".  Perhaps if you appear brave the crowd will be lenient
should you be so unfortunate as to lose a contest ...  There are small
unmarked doors.

Exits.Description: It seems the gladiators in the arena are looking at you and laughing.

The gladiators who are waiting to fight are snickering as they catch
sight of you.

Rooms.Name: Minotaurs
Rooms.Description:
Imported especially from Minos for the delight of the blood
thirsty Roman fans, the minotaurs in this holding pit have long,
sharp horns, and they know how to use them.  Far more dangerous than
the animals brought here to kill prisoners (and other hapless souls
who get in their path), these minotaurs have the intelligence to
fight a strong battle.

Exits.Description: There doesn't appear to be a doorknob on this side of the door.

Rooms.Name: Prisoners
Rooms.Description:
Execution as entertainment.  These prisoners have nothing to lose.
They know they are here to feed the lions, rhinoceri or whatever rare
beast happens to be on display in the arena today.  I don't think
this has put them in a very happy mood.  Better head back out north
from here.

Exits.Description:
A small plain wooden door has no doorknob on it on this side.  Hope
you didn't close the door when you came in here.
The floor is made of well packed dirt and clay.

Rooms.Name: Tigers, Oh My!
Rooms.Description:
Gold and black striped tigers brought here from the far reaches of
the empire pace restlessly back and forth, occasionally snarling with
their displeasure at being so caged.  Their long claws have made deep
indentations in the tall wooden post at the back of the cage.  Your
only way out of here is the small wooden door leading north.

Exits.Description:
A small plain wooden door has been built into the wall here.  It has no
knob on this side, however.

Rooms.Name: Tunnel Out
Rooms.Description:
A long, dark tunnel has been dug from the hard packed clay floors
of the prisoner's cell.  You can barely squeeze into it - those
prisoners are much more underfed than you - and you don't know
whether it has an ending in some place that you would like to be.  On
the other hand, how could it be worse than the pit of death of the
Arena?

Exits.Description:
Dim light strains into the tunnel from this direction.  The floor above
you is much too high to reach.
A strong stench has the unmistakable odor of raw sewage.

Rooms.Name: Lion Pit
Rooms.Description:
Like pampered pets, the lions are relatively well cared for.  The
pit that is their home while they are waiting for lunch is fairly large
but lit only by what faint daylight trickles in through a grilled
opening in one wall.  A small door leads south to the arena, but it has
no knob on this side.

Exits.Description:
A small wooden door is set into the wall, but it has no knob on this
side.

Rooms.Name: Pacing Panthers
Rooms.Description:
Sleek black panthers have been brought back from the far reaches
of the empire for the spectators' enjoyment.  The small holding area is
more like a cell, airless and dark.  During summer months it is an
oven, and during the winter it is damp and cold.  Just to the south you
can hear the noises of the gladiators' arena.

Exits.Description:
A small wooden door is set into the wall, but it has no knob on this
side.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
Long, rough wooden benches stretch endlessly around you, providing
seating for slaves and women.  You are far above the blood-soaked sand
where gladiators bravely die and wild animals are brutally slaughtered.
Seating continues to the north and south, or you may climb down into
the marble benches beneath you.

Exits.Description: Wooden benches provide seating for the likes of you.
Wooden benches provide seating for the likes of you.
Marble benches make a smooth if not soft cushion for your bottom.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
With your back to the southern wall of the arena, the gladiators and
animals look like tiny dolls far below you.  The wooden bench is rough
beneath you, and looks well weathered.  You are surrounded by the poor,
who are loudly yelling for their favorite in the deathly fight going on
below you.

Exits.Description: A sea of rough wooden benches has been set up for the likes of you.
A large dark door is marked with the single word "#rExit#N" (glowing).
A sea of rough wooden benches has been set up for women and slaves.
Rough seating lies further up.

The marble benches below you are no softer than the wooden ones, but
they are stronger and definitely more prestigious.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
From your vantage point high against the southern wall of the
Colosseum, the bloody battle far below you seems like those fantasies
you see at the theater, and not at all real.  The wooden benches
continue east and west of here, but you could climb down to the marble
benches.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
The Colosseum is a huge oval arena, providing entertainment for
50,000 screaming fans.  In the hot summer heat, canvas awnings are
rolled out to comfort even the women and the slaves as they watch
criminals being put to death or gladiators earning fame and glory.
If you don't like this vantage point, you can move north or east, or
try your luck in the more expensive seats.

Exits.Description: A small sign over a large doorway says "EXIT".

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
An endless sea of stone benches faces you.  There are no markers
to tell you precisely where your seat lies, and you can only go by the
glares of the other spectators to tell if you are in a section where
YOU are not ALLOWED.  Somewhere below you a to-the-death battle is
going on between man-and-man or man-and-beast.  If you don't find your
proper seat soon, you will be in a battle of your own.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
You are rapidly becoming lost in a seemingly endless circle of long
marble, stone and wooden benches.  This Colosseum is vast in size and
although you have seen many exits, you have yet to find your seat.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
Games and displays at this Colosseum have nearly made the elephant
in northern Africa, one of Rome's many provinces, extinct.  They have
also made the current government of Rome very popular.  Marble bench
(senatorial and noble) seating continues in most directions.

Exits.Description: Marble benches await the caress of your behind.
White marble benches surround the arena.

Patrician or plebeian, marble or wooden benches, the fans are just as
loud.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
An endless sea of stone benches faces you.  There are no markers
to tell you precisely where your seat lies, and you can only go by the
glares of the other spectators to tell if you are in a section where
YOU are not ALLOWED.  Somewhere below you a to-the-death battle is
going on between man-and-man or man-and-beast.  If you don't find your
proper seat soon, you will be in a battle of your own.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
Halfway up the eastern side of the Colosseum, you can easily hear
the gladiators' entering cry of, "Morituri te Salutant".  They look
quite brave, they who are about to die.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
You are among the poorest of Rome's populace, so high up that your
nose begins to bleed.  To your right, a vicious argument is breaking
out over an unpaid wager.  Far below you, a small group of criminals is
about to be torn apart by lions.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
The scent of incense from the Colosseum floor does not quite reach
this high, but the stench of blood and death does.  It excites those
around you, making them somewhat more aggressive than they might
otherwise be.

Rooms.Name: Colosseum Seating
Rooms.Description:
High up against the western wall of the Colosseum, you are glad to
miss the afternoon sun, which can be quite hot here despite the canvas
awning which is unfurled in early afternoon.  Wooden benches encircle
the Colosseum at this height, a haven for slaves and the poor.  There
is a large sign if you look north.

Exits.Description: There is a large sign here which says, "EXIT".

Rooms.Name: Temple of Jupiter
Rooms.Description:
Beautifully kept white marble steps lead up to an ornate portico
before an immense temple.  As you move towards the row of tall white
pillars lining the front of the temple, you look up to see statues over
the entrance move as if they were alive.

Exits.Description:
via Phobia is a busy street.  You hear vendors hawking their wares,
beggars begging, and all the noises of a big city.
Cool darkness prevents you from peering into the god's inner sanctum.

Rooms.Name: Temple of Jupiter
Rooms.Description:
The temple of Jupiter is dominated by an immense white marble statue
of the king of the Gods.  Jupiter manages to look both noble and
fierce, holding a thunderbolt in one hand with which to smite you, and
a staff in the other.  Do NOT make him angry.  He is quite fierce.

Rooms.Name: via Phobia by Jupiter
Rooms.Description:
via Phobia begins at the Forum just east of here and continues in its
broad path straight to the western gates of the city.  To the north you
can see the white stone steps to the temple of Vulcan.  Just to the
south lies the entrance to the temple to Jupiter.

Exits.Description: The wide marble steps provide entrance to the temple of Vulcan.

There seems to be some kind of sacrifice happening at the temple south
of here.

Rooms.Name: Temple of Mercury
Rooms.Description:
Signs of recent sacrifices to the cunning god of businessmen and
thieves are strewn about the temple floor.  Public celebrations are
held here, and once a year a huge banquet is held in his honor here.
From here you can look west and down to the busy via Rodentia.  Nearby
you hear the roar of crowds, thundering hooves, and the screams of the
dying.  Rome is truly an exciting place to be.

Exits.Description: via Rodentia lies just east of here.

The mysteries of the inner temple lie just through that enormous
archway.

Rooms.Name: Inside the Temple of Mercury
Rooms.Description:
An abundance of small, flat oil lamps does little to illuminate the
vast darkness of the inside of this temple.  God of trade and thieves,
the temple is supported by the wealthy businessmen of Rome, who give
10% of their profits for the upkeep of the shrine.

Exits.Description: An uncomfortable amount of sunlight pours in through the open doorway.

Rooms.Name: Temple of Vulcan
Rooms.Description:
